title: Playing with nouns and their forms
summary: Practise masculine and feminine gender, and singular and plural forms, in Spanish.
keyIdeas: Spanish nouns can be masculine, as in el gato, or feminine, as in la gata.
Singular names one thing, as in perro. Plural names more than one, as in perros.
Nouns agree with words such as el, la, los and las.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas la producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.explanation: We say la mesa, so mesa is feminine.
activities.hint: Try putting el or la before the word.

activities.explanation: Pelotas ends in -s and refers to more than one ball, so it is plural.

activities.prompt: Match each singular Spanish noun to its plural.
activities.explanation: These plurals add -s or -es. In pez → peces, z also changes to c.

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish nouns by their grammatical gender.
activities.explanation: We say el barco and el árbol (masculine), and la silla and la manzana (feminine).

activities.prompt: Choose the Spanish word that completes the sentence.
activities.explanation: Unas is feminine and plural, so we need fresas.
activities.sentence: Hugo y Aisha comen unas ___ rojas.

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish words by their number.
activities.explanation: Mochila and estuche name one object. Cuadernos and gomas name more than one.

activities.prompt: Which Spanish sentence contains an agreement mistake?
activities.explanation: Las is plural, but niña is singular. The correct phrase is las niñas.
activities.hint: Check whether the words that go together agree.
options: Las niña juegan en el parque.

activities.prompt: Order the Spanish sentence: first who (article and noun), then what they do, then how they sing.
activities.explanation: Start with capitalised Los, followed by pájaros and then cantan alto.

activities.prompt: Read the short Spanish story about the school garden and answer.
activities.explanation: The garden story has masculine and feminine nouns, in singular and plural forms.
activities.title: El huerto de 1º
activities.text: Omar y Lucía cuidan el huerto del colegio. Hoy riegan las plantas verdes. También recogen un tomate rojo y unas fresas dulces. Los niños están muy contentos con la cosecha.

questions.prompt: Which fruit or vegetable word is singular in the text?
questions.explanation: Un tomate names one tomato, so it is singular.

questions.prompt: Which word in the text is feminine and plural?
questions.explanation: We say las plantas. It is feminine and its -s marks the plural.

activities.prompt: Martina changes «el león fiero» to feminine and plural. Which is correct?
activities.explanation: The feminine of león is leona. In the plural, the phrase becomes las leonas fieras.
activities.hint: Change both the gender and the number.
